notes:
Top-line: mid-market product analytics SaaS. Evaluating Hosted API first to accelerate integration; strong interest in Dedicated after POC for predictable tail latency and data residency.

Key asks / quotes: "We need EU data to stay in-region for at-rest and in-use logs — legal will not accept pan-EU processing without clause." 

Technical constraints: p95 generation latency target ~<300ms for short chat prompts for EU users; peak throughput estimate ~150-250 rps for peak product notifications; cost sensitivity around token spend — asked about intelligent batching and cache suggestions.

Model preferences: prefer open/Redwood-verified LLMs (smaller base models for non-critical reranking) and automatic fallback to cheaper model for lower-priority requests. Wants routing policy: primary eu-west cluster for EU traffic, fallback to regionally nearest cluster with explicit latency/cost tradeoff.

Procurement: expects mid-Q2 decision if POC validates latency and legal residency SLA. Budget band ~75k-150k ARR.

Stubs/refs: Fireflies call ids and drive deck attached. Jira REDW-2123 opened for security clarifications.

AE notes (Maya): "Keep POC scope narrow — chat front-end + reranking test harness + residency proof-of-concept. Push Dedicated pricing with burst to hosted as hybrid option."
requirements_summary: Workload: interactive chat + embeddings + reranking. Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms EU. Throughput: 150-250 rps peak. Residency: EU-only storage of logs and audited access, legal clause required. Routing: multi-region routing with cost/latency policy, ability to pin EU traffic to Dedicated pool and failover to Hosted in emergencies. Security: SSO/SAML, SOC2, audit logs, KMS integration. Preferred models: Redwood-curated open models with fallback to smaller quantized variants for cost control.
notes_short: Mid-market EU SaaS; evaluating Hosted -> Dedicated; residency + latency are deal drivers. POC scoped; waiting on legal SLA and pricing approval.
